chemistry_plan.reaction_name: Photoredox Giese Radical Addition / Aerobic Sulfoxide Oxidation of PMPSCH2TMS
chemistry_plan.reaction_class: photoredox radical addition then photoredox aerobic oxidation
chemistry_plan.bond_formed: C–C (Giese addition of α-thio radical to acrylonitrile); S=O (sulfide to sulfoxide oxidation)
chemistry_plan.bond_broken: C–Si (homolytic/mesolytic cleavage of PMPSCH2TMS to generate α-thio radical); O=O (partial, O2 as terminal oxidant in Step 2)

feed_streams.reasoning: All reagents pre-mixed in pre-degassed EtOH/pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v) in a sealed reservoir under argon. Single feed avoids any air ingress from a second pump line. Pre-degassed offline per allowed oxygen exclusion method.

stages.solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v (pre-degassed offline under argon)

feed_streams.reasoning: Oxygen introduced via Bronkhorst O2 MFC as segmented gas-liquid flow into the Stage 1 effluent. This is the only new feed for Stage 2. The gas injection creates Taylor flow segments that enhance O2 mass transfer into the liquid.

stages.inlet_from_previous: Stage 1 outlet (sulfide intermediate 3a in EtOH/pH 9 buffer containing Ir photocatalyst)

reagents.name: PMPSCH2TMS
reagents.notes: para-methoxyphenyl thiomethyl trimethylsilane; limiting reagent at 0.1 M

reagents.name: acrylonitrile
reagents.notes: Volatile (bp 77 °C); BPR required to prevent outgassing

reagents.name: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6
reagents.notes: Iridium(III) photocatalyst; E1/2(III*/II) ~+1.21 V vs SCE; λ_abs MLCT band ~380–460 nm; used in both steps

reagents.name: O2
reagents.notes: Introduced only at Stage 2 via MFC; must be absent in Stage 1

reagents.name: pH 9 aqueous buffer
reagents.notes: Suppresses PMPSCH3 byproduct formation; pre-degassed offline

mechanism_steps.description: Photoexcitation of Ir(III) photocatalyst to generate *Ir(III) excited state upon absorption of 450 nm photon
Oxidative quenching of *Ir(III) by PMPSCH2TMS via single-electron transfer, generating PMPSCH2TMS radical cation and Ir(II)
Mesolytic C–Si bond cleavage of PMPSCH2TMS radical cation to release TMSI-equivalent and generate α-thio carbon radical PMPSCH2•
Giese radical addition: PMPSCH2• adds to acrylonitrile to form α-cyano radical adduct
Reduction of α-cyano radical adduct by Ir(II) to regenerate Ir(III) ground state and form carbanion, which is protonated to give sulfide intermediate 3a
Step 2: Photoexcitation of Ir(III) and generation of singlet oxygen or superoxide from O2 via energy/electron transfer; oxidation of sulfide 3a to sulfoxide 4a

chemistry_plan.energy_transfer_or_redox: oxidative quenching (Step 1); energy transfer to O2 or reductive quenching with O2 (Step 2)

stream_logic.reasoning: All liquid-phase reagents combined in a single pre-degassed feed to minimize O2 ingress. Catalyst is homogeneous and soluble at 0.5 mol% in EtOH/buffer. Pre-mixing is safe as no reaction occurs without light.

O2 gas introduced at Stage 2 inlet via Bronkhorst MFC into the Stage 1 liquid effluent. Stoichiometric O2 needed is ~1 equiv for sulfide→sulfoxide (requires 1 O-atom), but excess O2 gas is used to ensure saturation. Flow rate set by MFC.

chemistry_plan.mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A is a single pre-mixed, pre-degassed liquid feed containing substrate, acceptor, and photocatalyst — no mixing order concern since no reaction occurs in the dark. Stream B (O2 gas) is introduced only after Stage 1 is complete, at the T-junction between Stage 1 exit and Stage 2 reactor entrance.
chemistry_plan.deoxygenation_reasoning: Stage 1 requires strictly anaerobic conditions. O2 quenches the α-thio carbon radical intermediate, preventing Giese addition and promoting byproducts. Pre-degassed solvent prepared offline in sealed reservoir under argon is the allowed method (no inline degasser available).
chemistry_plan.batch_limitations_reasoning: mass_transfer_gas_liquid: matched [gas_liquid_phase_implies_kLa_limit]; photon_penetration: matched [photon delivery, photon flux]
chemistry_plan.wavelength_reasoning: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 has MLCT absorption band spanning ~380–460 nm with efficient intersystem crossing to triplet. Batch protocol uses 452 nm. The Vapourtec UV-150 450 nm module (measured 450 nm, 24 W radiant, 355 mW/cm²) is the best available match and provides the highest radiant power among compatible flow light sources.
chemistry_plan.confidence_notes: O2 equiv for Stage 2 is not explicitly stated in the protocol (batch used ambient air); 2.0 equiv is an estimate — MFC setpoint will need optimization. The UV-150 minimum operating temperature is 35 °C (with additional cooling), which is 10 °C above the batch protocol's 25 °C; this slight temperature increase should be acceptable and may even accelerate the reaction. The protocol does not specify whether the aerobic oxidation proceeds via singlet oxygen (energy transfer) or superoxide (electron transfer); both are possible with this Ir catalyst. Residence time reduction targets are model inference based on improved photon delivery, not measured data.

intensification_mandate.flow_justification_basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).

batch_record.reaction_description: One-pot photoredox Giese radical addition (Step 1, argon, 4 h) followed by aerobic oxidation (Step 2, open to air, 6 h). Substrate PMPSCH2TMS undergoes radical addition to acrylonitrile to give sulfide intermediate 3a, which is then oxidized to sulfoxide 4a. pH 9 aqueous buffer suppresses PMPSCH3 byproduct formation. Light and photocatalyst are essential for both steps.
batch_record.atmosphere: Step 1: argon (strictly oxygen-free, sealed pressure tube); Step 2: air (vessel opened after Step 1)
batch_record.raw_text:
Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.

Light and photocatalyst are essential for both steps.",

  "raw_text": "Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.\n\nSubstrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv\nMichael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv\nPhotocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%\nSolvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v\nConcentration: 0.1 M\nScale: 0.2 mmol\n\nStep 1 - Giese radical addition:\nThe reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free\nconditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 \u00b0C for\n4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a\nin 92% yield.\n\nStep 2 - Aerobic oxidation:\nAfter Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was\ncontinued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 \u00b0C for another\n6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.\n\nTotal batch reaction time: 10 hours\nFinal isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%\n\nCritical requirements:\n- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.\n- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.\n- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.\n- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct."
